apps.name: Collabora Online
apps.description: Edit Word, Excel and PowerPoint files in the browser, together, from a file app that opens it (OpenCloud). LibreOffice underneath, from Collabora's own packages.

env.desc: The address of the file app allowed to open documents here, like cloud.example.com

files.run:
#!/bin/sh
set -e
# coolwsd runs as this app's user, not the package's cool user, with its working folders in data/.
# No capabilities or mount namespaces in nook's sandbox, so each document is isolated by Landlock instead.
mkdir -p "$HOME/data/child-roots" "$HOME/data/cache"
hosts=""
i=0
for h in $(echo "$WOPI_HOSTS" | tr ',' ' ') 127.0.0.1; do
  hosts="$hosts --o:storage.wopi.host[$i]=$(echo "$h" | sed 's/[.]/\\./g')"
  i=$((i + 1))
done
exec /usr/bin/coolwsd --disable-cool-user-checking --port="$PORT" \
  --o:net.listen=loopback --o:net.proto=IPv4 \
  --o:ssl.enable=false --o:ssl.termination=true \
  --o:server_name="$SITE_HOST" \
  --o:child_root_path="$HOME/data/child-roots" --o:cache_files.path="$HOME/data/cache" \
  --o:mount_jail_tree=false --o:security.capabilities=false \
  --o:admin_console.enable=false --o:logging.file[@enable]=false \
  $hosts

apps.name: GoatCounter
apps.description: Privacy-friendly web analytics: page views, referrers and screen sizes without tracking people.

screenshots.alt: A week of page views, one chart per page
Total visits, top referrers, browsers and systems

env.desc: Your login, made on the first start
Your password (at least 8 characters)

files.run:
#!/bin/sh
set -e
# not GOATCOUNTER_*: GoatCounter reads those as its own flags and refuses names it doesn't know
mkdir -p "$HOME/data"
DB="sqlite+$HOME/data/goatcounter.sqlite3"
# make the site and its login before serving: until a site exists, GoatCounter offers anyone a sign-up form
if [ ! -f "$HOME/data/goatcounter.sqlite3" ]; then
  ./goatcounter db create site -createdb -db "$DB" -vhost "$SITE_HOST" -user.email "$GC_ADMIN_EMAIL" -user.password "$GC_ADMIN_PASSWORD"
fi
exec ./goatcounter serve -automigrate -listen "127.0.0.1:$PORT" -tls http -db "$DB"

apps.name: ntfy
apps.description: Push notifications to phones and desktops over plain HTTP PUT/POST. Also a target for nook's own update alerts.

env.desc: Public URL of this server
read-write, read-only, write-only or deny-all for anyone without a login

files.deprovision.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Called by nook when a notify binding goes: its login and tokens go; the topic's messages stay until they expire.
set -eu
export NTFY_AUTH_FILE="$HOME/data/ntfy/auth.db"
./ntfy user del "nook-$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
files.provision.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Called by nook when an app is bound to notify: a topic named after the app, and a login (nook-APP) that may only
# publish to it. Subscribe to the topic in the ntfy app to get what it sends.
set -eu
APP="$1"
U="nook-$APP"
export NTFY_AUTH_FILE="$HOME/data/ntfy/auth.db"
mkdir -p "$HOME/data/ntfy"
if ! ./ntfy user list 2>&1 | grep -q "^user $U "; then
  NTFY_PASSWORD=$(head -c 24 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n') ./ntfy user add "$U" >/dev/null
fi
./ntfy access "$U" "$APP" write-only >/dev/null
TOKEN=$(./ntfy token add "$U" 2>&1 | grep -o 'tk_[A-Za-z0-9]*' | head -n 1)
if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
  echo "ntfy didn't make a token for $U" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "NOTIFY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/$APP"
echo "NOTIFY_TOKEN=$TOKEN"
files.run:
#!/bin/sh
set -e
mkdir -p "$HOME/data/ntfy/attachments"
export NTFY_LISTEN_HTTP="127.0.0.1:$PORT"
export NTFY_BEHIND_PROXY=true
export NTFY_CACHE_FILE="$HOME/data/ntfy/cache.db"
export NTFY_AUTH_FILE="$HOME/data/ntfy/auth.db"
export NTFY_ATTACHMENT_CACHE_DIR="$HOME/data/ntfy/attachments"
exec ./ntfy serve

notify.desc: a topic named after each bound app, and a login that may only publish to it

apps.name: OpenCloud
apps.description: Files for a team: folders, sharing, sync clients for desktop and phone, and, with Collabora Online bound, office documents edited in the browser. One Go binary, no database.

env.desc: The admin user's password, set on the first start
Collabora Online's address, like https://office.example.com, to edit office documents (optional)

files.csp.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# OpenCloud's content security policy with Collabora's address allowed in frames
cat <<EOF
directives:
  child-src: ["'self'"]
  connect-src: ["'self'", "blob:"]
  default-src: ["'none'"]
  font-src: ["'self'"]
  frame-ancestors: ["'self'"]
  frame-src: ["'self'", "blob:", "$1/"]
  img-src: ["'self'", "data:", "blob:", "$1/"]
  manifest-src: ["'self'"]
  media-src: ["'self'"]
  object-src: ["'self'", "blob:"]
  script-src: ["'self'", "'unsafe-inline'"]
  style-src: ["'self'", "'unsafe-inline'"]
EOF
files.run:
#!/bin/sh
set -e
export OC_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/data/config" OC_BASE_DATA_PATH="$HOME/data/opencloud"
export OC_URL="https://$SITE_HOST" PROXY_TLS=false PROXY_HTTP_ADDR="127.0.0.1:$PORT" OC_LOG_LEVEL=warn
mkdir -p "$OC_CONFIG_DIR" "$OC_BASE_DATA_PATH"
if [ ! -f "$OC_CONFIG_DIR/opencloud.yaml" ]; then
  ./opencloud init --insecure no --admin-password "$OC_ADMIN_PASSWORD"
fi
if [ -n "$COLLABORA_URL" ]; then
  # the collaboration service speaks WOPI to Collabora on this server; the browser frames Collabora's own address
  export OC_ADD_RUN_SERVICES=collaboration COLLABORATION_APP_NAME=CollaboraOnline COLLABORATION_APP_PRODUCT=Collabora
  export COLLABORATION_APP_ADDR="$COLLABORA_URL" COLLABORATION_WOPI_SRC=http://127.0.0.1:9300 COLLABORATION_HTTP_ADDR=127.0.0.1:9300
  ./csp.sh "$COLLABORA_URL" > "$OC_CONFIG_DIR/csp.yaml"
  export PROXY_CSP_CONFIG_FILE_LOCATION="$OC_CONFIG_DIR/csp.yaml"
fi
exec ./opencloud server

env.desc: Email for the first superuser, made on the first start
Password for the first superuser (at least 8 characters). Change it later in the dashboard.

files.run:
#!/bin/sh
set -e
# everything PocketBase keeps lives in data/, which survives updates
D="$HOME/data"
mkdir -p "$D/pb_data" "$D/pb_public" "$D/pb_hooks" "$D/pb_migrations"
flags="--dir=$D/pb_data --publicDir=$D/pb_public --hooksDir=$D/pb_hooks --migrationsDir=$D/pb_migrations"
if [ ! -f "$D/pb_data/.superuser-made" ]; then
  ./pocketbase superuser upsert "$PB_ADMIN_EMAIL" "$PB_ADMIN_PASSWORD" $flags
  touch "$D/pb_data/.superuser-made"
fi
exec ./pocketbase serve --http="127.0.0.1:$PORT" $flags

apps.name: PostgreSQL
apps.description: A PostgreSQL server your apps share: each app that needs postgres gets a login and a database of its own, and only sees DATABASE_URL. Pick the major version; each runs as its own app, so 16 and 17 can sit side by side.

files.deprovision.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Called by nook when a binding goes: the login stops working; the database stays until you drop it.
set -eu
NAME="app_$(printf %s "$1" | tr - _)"
/usr/lib/postgresql/{version}/bin/psql -h "$HOME/data/run" -p "$PORT" -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -qtAc "alter role $NAME nologin" >/dev/null
files.export.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Called by nook when an app moves to another Postgres (nook-admin migrate): its database, to stdout.
set -eu
NAME="app_$(printf %s "$1" | tr - _)"
exec /usr/lib/postgresql/{version}/bin/pg_dump -h "$HOME/data/run" -p "$PORT" -Fc --no-owner --no-privileges "$NAME"
files.import.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Called by nook when an app moves here from another Postgres: its database from stdin, into the empty one
# provision.sh just made, owned by the app's login. Refuses a database that already has tables.
set -eu
NAME="app_$(printf %s "$1" | tr - _)"
BIN=/usr/lib/postgresql/{version}/bin
TABLES=$("$BIN/psql" -h "$HOME/data/run" -p "$PORT" -d "$NAME" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -qtAc \
  "select count(*) from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace where c.relkind in ('r', 'p', 'v', 'm', 'S') and n.nspname not in ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema') and n.nspname not like 'pg_toast%'")
if [ "$TABLES" != 0 ]; then
  echo "$NAME already has $TABLES tables here; not mixing the copy into it" >&2
  exit 1
fi
exec "$BIN/pg_restore" -h "$HOME/data/run" -p "$PORT" -d "$NAME" --no-owner --no-privileges --role="$NAME" --exit-on-error --single-transaction
files.provision.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Called by nook when an app is bound: a login and a database of its own, and its DATABASE_URL.
set -eu
APP="$1"
BIN=/usr/lib/postgresql/{version}/bin
NAME="app_$(printf %s "$APP" | tr - _)"
PW=$(head -c 32 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
q() { "$BIN/psql" -h "$HOME/data/run" -p "$PORT" -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -qtAc "$1"; }
if [ "$(q "select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = '$NAME'")" = 1 ]; then
  q "alter role $NAME with login password '$PW'" >/dev/null
else
  q "create role $NAME login password '$PW'" >/dev/null
fi
[ "$(q "select 1 from pg_database where datname = '$NAME'")" = 1 ] || q "create database $NAME owner $NAME" >/dev/null
echo "DATABASE_URL=postgres://$NAME:$PW@127.0.0.1:$PORT/$NAME"
files.run:
#!/bin/sh
# PostgreSQL {version} as a nook app: its cluster in data/pg, owned by this app's user, on $PORT (127.0.0.1 only)
# and a socket only this user can reach, for the provision scripts.
set -eu
BIN=/usr/lib/postgresql/{version}/bin
DATA="$HOME/data/pg"
SOCK="$HOME/data/run"
mkdir -p "$SOCK"
chmod 700 "$SOCK"
if [ ! -s "$DATA/PG_VERSION" ]; then
  "$BIN/initdb" -D "$DATA" -U "$(id -un)" --auth-local=peer --auth-host=scram-sha-256 -E UTF8 --locale=C.UTF-8 >/dev/null
fi
exec "$BIN/postgres" -D "$DATA" -k "$SOCK" -p "$PORT" -c listen_addresses=127.0.0.1 -c unix_socket_permissions=0700

postgres.desc: PostgreSQL {version}: a login and a database per app
